scenes.intro: Hello Michael. What you're looking at is your financial plan drawn as your own home. Your financial health score is 26 out of 100, which is critical. Each room shows you where you stand today.
scenes.pillar_savings_and_cash_flow: Your plumbing is savings and monthly cash flow. It is broken. It scores 0 out of 25. You save $43,000 a year, but your cash flow runs about $8,336 a year short because retirement, near-term goals and your cash cushion all draw on the same income. One surprise bill can put your home purchase or your retirement saving at risk.
scenes.pillar_debt: The walls are your debt, and they are solid. They score 8 out of 10. Your $28,500 in debt is manageable, but the $3,500 credit card at 20% is your most expensive debt for its size. Paying it off faster would compete with your home purchase or retirement saving.
scenes.pillar_investments: The garden is your investments, and it is cracked. It scores 11 out of 25. Your $145,000 is mostly in stocks, 73.5%, while the mix you chose aims for 98%. That gap means your money may grow more slowly than the plan expects, which matters for retiring at 58.
scenes.pillar_liquidity_and_emergency_fund: The foundations are your emergency fund and cash, and they are broken. They score 4 out of 20. Your $30,000 covers 3.2 months of expenses, about $16,530 short of the low end of the 5 to 6 month reserve you need. That cushion is what stands between you and a surprise bill or a pause in your income.
scenes.pillar_insurance_and_protection: The roof is your insurance and protection, and it is broken. It scores 4 out of 20. You have $180,000 of life insurance against a recommended $900,000 to $1,800,000, a $720,000 shortfall, and no umbrella policy, the extra cover for a big lawsuit. If your income stopped, the debts and plans you carry would be left without a backstop.
scenes.move_1: This step adds $1M of umbrella cover, the extra protection if someone sues you. It repairs your roof. Your score moves from 26 out of 100 to 31 out of 100.
scenes.move_2: This step means taking less out of your savings each year, $10,300 a year, which is 6.0%. It repairs your plumbing. Your score rises from 26 out of 100 to 62 out of 100.
scenes.move_3: This step moves more of your invested mix into stocks, from 74% to 88%. It repairs your garden. Your score goes from 26 out of 100 to 31 out of 100.
scenes.timeline: Looking ahead, you plan to retire at 58. The plan has your debts paid off by 2057, and your savings and investments run out at age 85. About $32,439 of planned spending would go unpaid by the end. That is the gap between the life you plan and what the current numbers support.
